title: Tech Note: Fuzzy Matching in 4th Dimension
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: This note is the deepest of a three-part FuzzyTools series, covering the theory of approximate string matching, real-world scenarios motivating fuzzy record matching, and the internal source-code architecture (protected gateway routines with input-validation "contracts" calling private worker routines, plus self-testing routines) of the FuzzyTools component. The computer-science content — phonetic transcription and edit-distance/LCS theory, and the gateway/contract software design pattern — is timeless and still directly applicable to any language including modern 4D, but the concrete artifact (the FuzzyTools component and its specific method names) is a 2006-era third-party add-on tied to the classic procedural 4D language, well before 4D's SQL engine or ORDA existed.
related_updates: FuzzyTools is a third-party/community 4D component from 2006, not part of any current 4D distribution
The referenced companion note 'Scanning Text and BLOBs Efficiently' (TN 05-42) is likewise a period-specific performance note for classic 4D BLOB/text handling
